chapter_text:
CHAPTER 15 — ईशः क्व अस्ति (ISHAH KVA ASTI) — "Where is God?"

Introduction — पाठ-परिचयः

One of the oldest questions a thoughtful person can ask is 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?' — 'Where is God?' The Sanskrit word ईश (isha) means 'the Lord', 'the ruler', the supreme power behind the universe; क्व means 'where' and अस्ति means 'is'. This lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) does not try to prove or disprove anything; it presents, in the cultural-literary tradition of India, one classical answer — that the divine is not shut up in any single place but pervades the whole world and dwells within every living being. This idea is called सर्वव्यापकता (omnipresence): ईश is सर्वत्र, everywhere.

We approach the theme in three ways. First, through a simple guru-shishya dialogue (गुरु-शिष्य-संवादः) retold in easy Sanskrit prose, in which a teacher answers a pupil's question with a salt-and-water demonstration. Second, through four authentic public-domain verses — one from the ईशावास्य-उपनिषद् (Isha Upanishad) and three from the भगवद्गीता (Bhagavad Gita) — with word-meanings and English translations. Third, through a short grammar section (व्याकरणम्) that draws सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप out of the very words we read. Throughout, the tone is educational and reflective, inviting the student to think about how the idea of a divine-in-all shapes values such as compassion (दया), non-greed and service (सेवा).

Why the question matters (प्रश्नस्य महत्त्वम्)

A small child points to the sky and asks where God lives. A scientist asks what holds the universe together. A poet feels a presence in a river, a mountain, a kind act. The Sanskrit tradition gathered such wonder into a single, memorable answer: the divine is the inmost reality of everything. If that is so, then the question 'Where is God?' quietly turns into another question — 'How then should I live?' For if the same divine dwells in all, every being deserves respect, and helping others becomes a form of worship. This is why the theme has been taught to the young for centuries: it is at once a lesson about the world and a lesson about character.

Part 1 — गुरु-शिष्य-संवादः (The dialogue of teacher and pupil)

(Simple Sanskrit prose, retold for learners — not a textbook copy.)

एकदा एकः जिज्ञासुः शिष्यः गुरुम् अपृच्छत् — "भगवन्, ईशः क्व अस्ति? अहं तं द्रष्टुम् इच्छामि।"
गुरुः स्मितं कृत्वा अवदत् — "वत्स, ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति। सः जले, स्थले, वृक्षे, पर्वते, वायौ, सर्वेषु प्राणिषु च वसति।"
शिष्यः अवदत् — "किन्तु अहं तं न पश्यामि। यदि सः सर्वत्र अस्ति, तर्हि सः अदृश्यः कथम्?"
गुरुः किमपि न उक्त्वा जलपूर्णम् एकं पात्रम् आनयत्। सः तस्मिन् जले किञ्चित् लवणम् अक्षिपत्, "श्वः पुनः आगच्छ" इति च अवदत्।
श्वः शिष्यः आगच्छत्। गुरुः अपृच्छत् — "यत् लवणं ह्यः अक्षिपम्, तत् आनय।" शिष्यः जले लवणम् अन्विष्यत्, किन्तु तत् न अपश्यत्। "गुरो, लवणं तु न दृश्यते" इति सः अवदत्।
गुरुः अवदत् — "जलम् आस्वादय।" शिष्यः जलम् आस्वादयत्। गुरुः अपृच्छत् — "कीदृशम्?" शिष्यः अवदत् — "लवणयुक्तम्, गुरो! सर्वत्र मधुरम् इव लवणरसः अस्ति।"
गुरुः शान्तस्वरेण अवदत् — "पश्य वत्स। लवणं न दृश्यते, तथापि सर्वस्मिन् जले व्याप्तम् अस्ति; तत् त्वं रसेन जानासि। एवमेव ईशः अदृश्यः, तथापि सर्वस्मिन् जगति व्याप्तः अस्ति। यः सर्वभूतेषु ईशं पश्यति, यः च सर्वेषु प्राणिषु दयां करोति, सः एव सत्यम् ईशं भजते।"
शिष्यः प्रणम्य अवदत् — "अवगतम्, गुरो! ईशं द्रष्टुं बहिः गन्तुं न आवश्यकम्; सर्वभूतेषु एव सः वर्तते। अतः सेवा एव पूजा।"

शब्दार्थ (word meanings): जिज्ञासुः = eager to know; अपृच्छत् = asked; द्रष्टुम् इच्छामि = I wish to see; सर्वत्र = everywhere; वसति = dwells; प्राणिषु = in living beings; अदृश्यः = invisible; जलपूर्णम् पात्रम् = a pot full of water; लवणम् = salt; अक्षिपत् = threw/dropped; श्वः = tomorrow / the next day; आनय = bring; अन्विष्यत् = searched for; न दृश्यते = is not seen; आस्वादय = taste; लवणयुक्तम् = mixed with salt (salty); व्याप्तम् = pervaded, spread through; रसेन जानासि = you know (it) by taste; भजते = worships; प्रणम्य = having bowed; वर्तते = exists/is present; सेवा = service; पूजा = worship.

English translation: One day an eager pupil asked his teacher, "Sir, where is God? I wish to see Him." The teacher smiled and said, "Child, God is everywhere. He dwells in water, land, tree, mountain, wind and in all living beings." The pupil said, "But I do not see Him. If He is everywhere, how is He invisible?" Without a word the teacher brought a pot full of water, dropped a little salt into it, and said, "Come again tomorrow." The next day the pupil came. The teacher asked, "Bring me the salt I put in yesterday." The pupil searched in the water but could not find it. "Sir, the salt is not to be seen," he said. The teacher said, "Taste the water." The pupil tasted it. "How is it?" asked the teacher. "It is salty, sir — the taste of salt is everywhere in it." The teacher said gently, "See, child. The salt is not seen, yet it has spread through all the water; you know it by its taste. In just this way God is invisible, yet He pervades the whole world. One who sees God in all beings, and who shows compassion to all creatures, truly worships God." The pupil bowed and said, "I understand, sir. One need not go outside to see God; He is present in all beings. Therefore service itself is worship."

Moral (सारः): God's presence is like the salt dissolved in water — unseen, yet everywhere; it is known not by the eye but by its 'taste', that is, by the goodness and life we meet in all beings. The dialogue turns the question 'Where is God?' into a way of living: see the divine in every creature and serve all with compassion. सेवा एव पूजा — service itself is worship. (This retelling follows the spirit of the well-known salt-in-water teaching of the Chandogya Upanishad but is written afresh in simple words.)

Part 2 — प्रमुख-श्लोकाः (Four verses with meanings)

1) ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् ।
   तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥ (ईशावास्य-उपनिषद् 1)
   शब्दार्थ: ईश-आवास्यम् = to be enveloped/indwelt by the Lord; इदम् = this; सर्वम् = all; यत् किञ्च = whatever; जगत्याम् = in the world; जगत् = that which moves; तेन त्यक्तेन = by that renunciation / by letting go; भुञ्जीथाः = you should enjoy; मा गृधः = do not covet; कस्यस्वित् = of anyone; धनम् = wealth.
   Translation: All this — whatever moves in this moving world — is pervaded (enveloped) by the Lord. Therefore enjoy (your portion) through renunciation; do not covet the wealth of anyone.
   Idea: Divine omnipresence plus an ethic of non-greed — because everything belongs to ईश, live with contentment.

2) समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
   ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥ (भगवद्गीता 9.29)
   शब्दार्थ: समः = equal, same; अहम् = I; सर्वभूतेषु = in/toward all beings; द्वेष्यः = hateful; प्रियः = dear; ये = those who; भजन्ति = worship; मां = me; भक्त्या = with devotion; मयि = in me; ते = they; तेषु = in them; च = and; अपि = also.
   Translation: I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me and none especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
   Idea: Divine equality — the same presence in all, with no partiality.

3) ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
   भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ (भगवद्गीता 18.61)
   शब्दार्थ: ईश्वरः = the Lord; सर्वभूतानाम् = of all beings; हृद्देशे = in the region of the heart; अर्जुन = O Arjuna; तिष्ठति = dwells/remains; भ्रामयन् = causing to revolve; सर्वभूतानि = all beings; यन्त्र-आरूढानि = mounted as if on a machine; मायया = by (his) power/माया.
   Translation: The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to move as if mounted on a machine, by his power.
   Idea: The divine is not far away but within the heart of every being.

4) यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।
   तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ (भगवद्गीता 6.30)
   शब्दार्थ: यः = who; मां = me; पश्यति = sees; सर्वत्र = everywhere; सर्वम् = all; मयि = in me; तस्य = to/of him; अहम् = I; न प्रणश्यामि = am not lost; सः = he; मे = to me; न प्रणश्यति = is not lost.
   Translation: One who sees me everywhere and sees all things in me — to him I am never lost, and he is never lost to me.
   Idea: Seeing the divine everywhere keeps one ever close to the divine.

Part 3 — व्याकरणम् (Grammar drawn from the words)

(A) सन्धि (the joining of sounds). Where two sounds meet in Sanskrit they often merge and change. From our lesson:
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि (a short vowel + a like vowel → one long vowel): न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ).
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि (visarga ः before अ → ओ): समः + अहम् = समोऽहम्; ईश्वरः + अर्जुन = ईश्वरोऽर्जुन. The lost अ is marked by the sign अवग्रह (ऽ).
  • अनुस्वार (म् before a consonant → ं): इदम् + सर्वम् = इदं सर्वम्.
  Splitting a joined form back into parts is called सन्धि-विच्छेद (e.g., नास्ति = न + अस्ति). Both joining and splitting are needed to read verses correctly.

(B) विभक्ति (case endings). A noun's ending shows its role. Examples from the lesson, using the pattern of देव / ईश (masculine a-stem):
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): ईशः 'the Lord', ईश्वरः 'the Lord'.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): ईशम् 'God (as object)', लवणम् 'salt'.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): भक्त्या 'by devotion', रसेन 'by taste'.
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from'): जलात् 'from water'.
  • षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): सर्वभूतानाम् 'of all beings'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at'): जले 'in the water', सर्वभूतेषु 'in all beings', हृद्देशे 'in the heart'.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension). The masculine a-stem देव declines in the प्रथमा (nominative) as: एकवचन देवः (one), द्विवचन देवौ (two), बहुवचन देवाः (many). The same pattern gives ईशः / ईशौ / ईशाः. In the verses, ईशः and ईश्वरः are singular nominatives (the subject), while सर्वभूतानि (all beings) is a neuter plural object.

(D) धातुरूप (verb forms, present लट् लकार, 3rd person). From the lesson:
  • अस् (to be): अस्ति 'is' (एकवचन), सन्ति 'are' (बहुवचन).
  • वस् (to dwell): वसति 'dwells', वसन्ति 'dwell'.
  • स्था (to stand/remain): तिष्ठति 'remains/dwells'.
  • दृश् (to see): पश्यति 'sees'.
  • भज् (to worship/serve): भजते 'worships' (आत्मनेपद).
Notice how these small verbs carry the whole meaning of the lesson: ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति, सर्वभूतेषु वसति, हृद्देशे तिष्ठति; यः तं पश्यति सः तं भजते.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you explored the old question 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?' — Where is God? — and one classical, cultural answer: the divine (ईश) is not confined to a single place but pervades the whole world and dwells within all beings (सर्वव्यापकता, omnipresence). Through a simple guru-shishya dialogue you saw how a teacher explained this with salt dissolved in water: unseen, yet present everywhere, known by its 'taste'. Through four public-domain verses — ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम् (Isha Upanishad), समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु and ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे and यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र (Bhagavad Gita) — you met the ideas of divine pervasion, divine equality, the God-within-the-heart, and seeing the divine everywhere. From the same words you drew grammar: सन्धि (नास्ति, समोऽहम्) and सन्धि-विच्छेद, the six विभक्ति with examples, the शब्दरूप of देव/ईश, and the धातुरूप of अस्, वस्, स्था, दृश्, भज्. The lesson's quiet conclusion is practical as well as reflective: if the one divine dwells in all, then compassion, non-greed and service naturally follow — सेवा एव पूजा, service itself is worship.

topics.name: ईशः क्व अस्ति — The Question of Divine Omnipresence
topics.description: The chapter's central question 'Where is God?' and its classical cultural answer: the divine (ईश) is not confined to one place but pervades the whole world and dwells within all beings (सर्वव्यापकता / omnipresence).

topics.name: गुरु-शिष्य-संवादः — The Salt-in-Water Dialogue
topics.description: A simple guru-shishya dialogue retold in easy Sanskrit prose, in which a teacher answers the pupil's question with a salt-and-water demonstration showing how the unseen can still be everywhere; with शब्दार्थ, translation and moral.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary from the lesson: ईश, सर्वम्, जगत्, भूत, हृदय, लवण, जल, सेवा, पूजा, दया, सर्वत्र, अदृश्य, व्याप्त and their English meanings and case-forms.

topics.name: प्रमुख-श्लोकाः — Verses from the Isha Upanishad and Bhagavad Gita
topics.description: Four authentic public-domain verses — ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम् (Isha Upanishad) and समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु, ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे, यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र (Bhagavad Gita) — with word meanings and translations.

topics.name: मूल्यानि — Devotional and Moral Themes
topics.description: The values carried by the theme: divine omnipresence and equality, seeing God in all creation, compassion (दया) toward all beings, non-greed (मा गृधः), and service as worship (सेवा एव पूजा).

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Lesson
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the words: सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद (नास्ति, समोऽहम्, इदं सर्वम्), the six विभक्ति case endings with examples, the शब्दरूप of देव/ईश, and the धातुरूप of अस्, वस्, स्था, दृश्, भज्.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: ईशः क्व अस्ति — The Question of Divine Omnipresence
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the chapter's central idea — that the divine (ईश) dwells everywhere and within all beings (omnipresence) — and answer the question 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?'.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: प्रमुख-श्लोकाः — Verses from the Isha Upanishad and Bhagavad Gita
learning_outcomes.description: Recall and recite the four key public-domain verses of the lesson and identify each by its opening words and source (Isha Upanishad / Bhagavad Gita).
Narrate the guru-shishya salt-in-water dialogue and explain how the demonstration shows the unseen, all-pervading presence of ईश.
Give the शब्दार्थ (word meaning) in English of Sanskrit words drawn from the lesson and use the vocabulary correctly.
Analyse the devotional and moral themes of the lesson — omnipresence, divine equality, compassion, non-greed and service as worship — and apply them to everyday life.
Identify and perform simple सन्धि joins and सन्धि-विच्छेद (splits) using examples taken from the lesson.
Recognise the common विभक्ति case endings, the शब्दरूप of an a-stem noun, and the धातुरूप of key verbs, and state the case or verb-form of a word in the lesson.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: प्रमुख-श्लोकाः — Verses from the Isha Upanishad and Bhagavad Gita
learning_outcomes.description: Translate a given verse or sentence of the lesson into simple English and answer comprehension questions about its words, grammar and meaning.

chapter_summary.title: ईशः क्व अस्ति (Ishah Kva Asti) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 15. It explores the question 'Where is God?' and its classical cultural answer — that the divine (ईश) pervades the whole world and dwells within all beings — through a guru-shishya salt-in-water dialogue, four public-domain verses from the Isha Upanishad and Bhagavad Gita, and grammar (सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप, धातुरूप) drawn from the words.

branches.label: प्रश्नः — The Question
details: ईशः क्व अस्ति? = Where is God?

branches.label: संवादः — The Story
details: Unseen yet everywhere; known by taste
सेवा एव पूजा — service is worship

sections.heading: The central question and its answer
bullets: The chapter asks 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?' — Where is God? — and answers that ईश is सर्वत्र, everywhere.
The divine is not confined to a temple or the sky but pervades the whole world (सर्वव्यापकता / omnipresence) and dwells within all beings.
The question 'Where is God?' quietly becomes 'How then should I live?' — with respect for all beings.

sections.heading: The salt-in-water dialogue
bullets: A pupil asks the guru where God is and says he cannot see Him.
The guru dissolves salt (लवणम्) in water; the next day it cannot be seen, yet the water tastes salty everywhere.
Lesson: like the invisible salt, ईश is unseen yet pervades everything; 'सेवा एव पूजा' — service is worship.

sections.heading: Four verses and their ideas
bullets: ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम् (Isha Up. 1): all this is pervaded by the Lord — enjoy with renunciation, do not covet (मा गृधः).
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु (Gita 9.29): God is equal in all beings — no hatred, no favouritism.
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे (Gita 18.61): the Lord dwells in the heart of every being.
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र (Gita 6.30): one who sees God everywhere is never far from the divine.

sections.heading: Devotional and moral themes
bullets: Omnipresence and equality lead to treating all beings with equal respect.
Compassion (दया) to all creatures and care for nature follow from seeing the divine in all.
Non-greed and contentment: 'तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथाः, मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्'.
Service (सेवा) to others, especially the needy, is the truest worship (पूजा).

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धि: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (दीर्घ); समः + अहम् = समोऽहम् (visarga); इदम् + सर्वम् = इदं सर्वम् (anusvara); सन्धि-विच्छेद splits them back.
विभक्ति: सप्तमी जले / सर्वभूतेषु 'in'; षष्ठी सर्वभूतानाम् 'of'; तृतीया भक्त्या 'by'.
शब्दरूप of देव (प्रथमा): देवः / देवौ / देवाः.
धातुरूप (present): अस् → अस्ति; वस् → वसति; स्था → तिष्ठति; दृश् → पश्यति; भज् → भजते.

key_takeaways: The chapter answers 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?' — God is everywhere (सर्वत्र) and dwells within all beings.
The salt-in-water dialogue shows that the divine, like dissolved salt, is unseen yet pervades everything.
ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम्: all this world is pervaded by the Lord — live with renunciation and non-greed.
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु: God is equal in all beings, so we too should treat all with equal respect.
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे तिष्ठति: the divine dwells within the heart of every being.
Seeing God in all leads to compassion, and 'सेवा एव पूजा' — service itself is worship.
Grammar: नास्ति = न + अस्ति; सप्तमी 'in' (जले, सर्वभूतेषु); धातुरूप अस्ति / वसति / तिष्ठति.

glossary.definition: The Lord, the supreme power that pervades and rules all; the divine referred to throughout the chapter.
'Where'; the question-word in the chapter title 'ईशः क्व अस्ति' (Where is God?).
'Everywhere'; the chapter's answer to where the divine is.
Omnipresence — the quality of being present everywhere at once, ascribed to ईश.
'In all beings' (locative plural of सर्वभूत); used in the Gita verse समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु.
'In the region of the heart' (locative); where the Lord is said to dwell in Gita 18.61.
Salt; used in the guru's demonstration to show an unseen yet all-pervading presence.
Pervaded, spread through; describes how the salt fills the water and how ईश fills the world.
Service; in the lesson, service to all beings is held to be true worship (सेवा एव पूजा).
Worship; the lesson teaches that serving the divine-in-all is the truest form of worship.
Compassion, mercy; the natural attitude toward all beings when one sees the divine in them.
'Do not covet'; the Isha Upanishad's warning against greed for another's wealth.
The splitting of a joined (sandhi) form back into its separate words, e.g., नास्ति = न + अस्ति.
A noun's case ending showing its role, e.g., सप्तमी (locative) जले 'in the water'.
The conjugated form of a verb-root, e.g., वस् → वसति 'dwells', स्था → तिष्ठति 'remains'.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — ईशः क्व अस्ति (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 15)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses and the story in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Answer briefly: 'ईशः क्व अस्ति?' State the chapter's answer in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति — God is everywhere. The divine dwells in water, land, trees, mountains and in the hearts of all living beings; there is no place without God.

questions.question: Narrate briefly what the guru does with salt and water, and what the pupil learns.
questions.answer: The guru dissolves salt (लवणम्) in a pot of water. The next day the salt cannot be seen, yet the water tastes salty everywhere. The pupil learns that, like the invisible salt, ईश is unseen yet pervades everything.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: ईशः, लवणम्, सेवा, दया, सर्वत्र.
questions.answer: ईशः = the Lord/God; लवणम् = salt; सेवा = service; दया = compassion; सर्वत्र = everywhere.

questions.question: Write the verse 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु...' (first line) and explain what it teaches about God.
questions.answer: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः। It teaches that God is equal (समः) toward all beings — none is hateful and none specially favoured; the divine is present in all alike.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद: (a) नास्ति (b) समोऽहम्.
questions.answer: (a) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) समोऽहम् = समः + अहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि, ः + अ → ओ).

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and meaning of: जले, सर्वभूतेषु, सर्वभूतानाम्.
questions.answer: जले = सप्तमी (locative), 'in the water'. सर्वभूतेषु = सप्तमी (locative) plural, 'in all beings'. सर्वभूतानाम् = षष्ठी (genitive) plural, 'of all beings'.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे तिष्ठति।'
questions.answer: 'The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings.' God resides within the heart of every creature (Gita 18.61).

questions.question: Explain the theme 'सेवा एव पूजा' (service is worship) using ideas from the lesson, and give two ways a student can practise it.
questions.answer: Because ईश dwells within every being, serving and being kind to any creature honours the divine present in it; hence service (सेवा) itself becomes worship (पूजा). The salt-in-water dialogue ends with this very conclusion, and the Gita's 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु' supports it by teaching that the same divine is in all. Two ways a student can practise it: (1) help classmates, elders and the needy with kindness and without discrimination; (2) be gentle to animals and protect plants and nature. Such unselfish service expresses seeing God in all.

questions.question: Translate and explain: 'ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्। तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्॥'
questions.answer: Translation: 'All this — whatever moves in this moving world — is pervaded by the Lord; therefore enjoy (your share) through renunciation, do not covet anyone's wealth.' Explanation: the first line teaches divine omnipresence — everything is enveloped by ईश; the second draws the ethic of non-greed — since all belongs to the Lord, one should live with contentment and letting-go, never grabbing what belongs to others.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।
(a) Where does the Lord dwell? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'सर्वभूतानाम्'? (c) From which धातु is 'तिष्ठति'? (d) What idea does the line convey?
questions.answer: (a) In the heart-region (हृद्देश) of all beings. (b) सर्वभूतानाम् is षष्ठी (genitive) plural, 'of all beings'. (c) तिष्ठति is from the धातु स्था (to stand/remain). (d) It conveys that the divine dwells within the heart of every being.

questions.answer: ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति — God is everywhere. The divine (ईश) dwells in water, land, trees, mountains and in the hearts of all living beings; there is no place where God is not.
questions.explanation: States the core idea of omnipresence.

questions.question: Explain why the lesson says 'सेवा एव पूजा' (service itself is worship).
questions.answer: Because ईश dwells within every being, serving and being kind to any living creature is the same as worshipping God. When we help others with love and compassion (दया), we honour the divine that lives in them; hence service (सेवा) itself becomes true worship (पूजा).
questions.explanation: Links omnipresence to service as worship.

questions.question: Write the opening line of the Isha Upanishad taught in this lesson (in Devanagari) and give its meaning.
questions.answer: ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्। Meaning: All this — whatever moves in this moving world — is pervaded (enveloped) by the Lord (ईश).
questions.explanation: Recall of Isha Upanishad 1 with meaning.

questions.question: Write the Gita line 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु...' and explain what it teaches about God.
questions.answer: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः। It teaches that God is equal (समः) towards all beings — none is hateful and none is specially favoured. God shows no partiality; the divine is present in every creature alike.

questions.question: Briefly narrate what the guru does with salt and water in the story.
questions.answer: The guru drops some salt (लवणम्) into a pot of water and asks the pupil to return the next day. The salt cannot be seen, yet the water tastes salty everywhere — showing that the salt has spread invisibly through all the water.

questions.question: How does the salt-in-water example explain where God is?
questions.answer: Just as the salt becomes invisible yet is present in every drop of the water (known by its taste), ईश too is unseen yet pervades the whole world. God cannot be seen with the eyes but is present everywhere and in every being — that is the answer to 'ईशः क्व अस्ति'.
questions.explanation: Explains the analogy: unseen but all-pervading.

questions.question: Why is a simple demonstration a good way for the guru to teach this idea?
questions.answer: The idea of an invisible, all-pervading ईश is abstract and hard to grasp by words alone. By letting the pupil taste the water, the guru gives direct experience: the pupil himself discovers that something unseen can still be everywhere. Experience convinces more deeply than mere telling.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: ईशः, जलम्, लवणम्, सेवा.
questions.answer: ईशः = the Lord/God; जलम् = water; लवणम् = salt; सेवा = service.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: हृदयम्, दया, सर्वत्र, अदृश्यः.
questions.answer: हृदयम् = heart; दया = compassion/mercy; सर्वत्र = everywhere; अदृश्यः = invisible.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: व्याप्तः, प्राणी, समः, पूजा, गुरुः.
questions.answer: व्याप्तः = pervaded/spread through; प्राणी = a living being; समः = equal/same; पूजा = worship; गुरुः = teacher.

questions.question: How does believing that ईश is present in all beings change the way we treat others?
questions.answer: If God dwells in every being, then every person, animal and plant deserves respect and kindness. We stop dividing beings into 'liked' and 'hated', avoid harming others, and act with compassion (दया). Recognising the one divine in all naturally leads to honesty, service and care for nature.

questions.question: Explain the teaching 'मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्' and its value.
questions.answer: It means 'do not covet anyone's wealth.' Since all things belong to the all-pervading ईश, one should enjoy one's share with contentment and renunciation (तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथाः) rather than greedily grabbing what belongs to others. The value taught is non-greed and contentment.

questions.question: State two everyday actions by which a student can practise 'seeing God in all'.
questions.answer: 1) Helping and being kind to classmates, elders and strangers without discrimination. 2) Being gentle to animals and protecting plants and nature. Such acts treat the divine in all beings with respect.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split): (a) नास्ति (b) समोऽहम्.
questions.answer: (a) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) समोऽहम् = समः + अहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि; ः + अ → ओ, elided अ marked by ऽ).

questions.question: Join by सन्धि: (a) न + अस्ति (b) इदम् + सर्वम्.
questions.answer: (a) न + अस्ति = नास्ति. (b) इदम् + सर्वम् = इदं सर्वम् (म् → anusvara ं before a consonant).

questions.question: What is सन्धि, and what is सन्धि-विच्छेद? Give one example.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the merging of sounds where two words meet (e.g., न + अस्ति = नास्ति). सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words (नास्ति = न + अस्ति).

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and meaning of: सर्वभूतेषु, सर्वभूतानाम्.
questions.answer: सर्वभूतेषु = सप्तमी (locative) plural → 'in all beings'. सर्वभूतानाम् = षष्ठी (genitive) plural → 'of all beings'.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of देव (masculine) in प्रथमा — all three numbers.
questions.answer: प्रथमा (nominative): एकवचन देवः, द्विवचन देवौ, बहुवचन देवाः.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (लट् लकार, 3rd person) for अस्, वस् and स्था — singular forms.
questions.answer: अस् (to be) → अस्ति ('is'). वस् (to dwell) → वसति ('dwells'). स्था (to stand/remain) → तिष्ठति ('remains/stays').
questions.explanation: Verb forms used in the lesson.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे तिष्ठति।'
questions.answer: 'The Lord (ईश्वर) dwells in the heart-region (हृद्देश) of all beings (सर्वभूतानाम्).' It teaches that God resides within the heart of every creature.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'यः सर्वभूतेषु ईशं पश्यति सः सत्यम् ईशं भजते।'
questions.answer: 'One who sees God (ईश) in all beings truly worships God.' Seeing the divine in every being is real devotion.

questions.question: Write two simple Sanskrit sentences (Devanagari) expressing that God is everywhere, with English meanings.
questions.answer: 1) ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति। (God is everywhere.) 2) ईशः सर्वभूतेषु वसति। (God dwells in all beings.)

questions.question: Explain the central idea of the chapter 'ईशः क्व अस्ति' — where the divine dwells and how one should respond to that idea.
questions.answer:
The chapter answers the question 'Where is God?' (ईशः क्व अस्ति?) by teaching that the divine (ईश) is not confined to any single place but pervades the whole world — 'ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम्', all this is enveloped by the Lord. God dwells in water, land, trees, mountains and, above all, in the hearts of all living beings ('ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशे तिष्ठति'). Because God is unseen yet everywhere, one cannot point to God with a finger, just as one cannot see the salt dissolved in water though it fills every drop.
The proper response to this idea is to see the one divine in all creation and to act accordingly: to treat every being with respect and compassion, to avoid greed ('मा गृधः'), and to serve others — for 'सेवा एव पूजा', service itself is worship. Thus the lesson turns a question about God's location into a teaching about how to live: with reverence for all life.

questions.question: Narrate the guru-shishya dialogue of this lesson and explain the meaning of the salt-in-water demonstration.
questions.answer:
A pupil (शिष्य) once asked his teacher (गुरु), 'Sir, where is God? I wish to see Him.' The guru replied that ईश dwells everywhere — in water, land, tree, mountain and in all beings. The pupil objected that he could not see God at all. So the guru took a pot of water and dropped some salt (लवणम्) into it, asking the pupil to return the next day.
The next day the guru asked the pupil to bring back the salt. The pupil searched but could not find it in the water. The guru then asked him to taste the water; the pupil found it salty everywhere. The guru explained: 'The salt cannot be seen, yet it has spread through all the water — you know it by its taste. In the same way, ईश is invisible, yet He pervades the whole world and dwells in every being.'
The demonstration teaches that something unseen can still be fully present everywhere. God need not be visible to be real and near. The pupil bows and concludes 'सेवा एव पूजा' — since God is in all, serving all beings is the truest worship. The story thus answers 'ईशः क्व अस्ति' through direct experience rather than mere words.
questions.explanation: Full narration + interpretation of the analogy.

questions.question: Discuss the theme that 'the divine is equal in all beings' using the Gita verse 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु...', and explain how this idea can guide behaviour today.
questions.answer:
The verse 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः' declares that God is the same (समः) towards all beings — none is hateful (द्वेष्य) and none specially dear (प्रिय). The second half, 'ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्', adds that those who worship with devotion dwell in God, and God in them. The core idea is divine equality and nearness: the same divine presence lives in every creature.
This idea can guide behaviour in many ways today. If the same divine is in all, discrimination by birth, wealth, religion or appearance loses its ground; we are led to treat every person with equal respect. It encourages compassion (दया) toward the weak, kindness to animals, and care for nature. It fosters honesty, because cheating another is, in a sense, harming the divine within them. And it promotes service — helping a stranger becomes a form of worship. Thus a verse about God's equality becomes a practical charter for fairness, harmony and unselfish service.

questions.question: 'Seeing God everywhere makes a person kinder and less greedy.' Evaluate this statement using ideas from the lesson.
questions.answer:
The statement agrees with the lesson's message. First, kindness: if ईश dwells in all beings ('सर्वभूतेषु'), then hurting any being means disrespecting the divine within it; recognising this naturally makes a person gentle, compassionate and even-minded toward all. Second, less greed: the Isha verse says 'तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्' — enjoy through renunciation, do not covet another's wealth. Since everything belongs to the all-pervading Lord, grabbing more than one's share is meaningless; contentment replaces greed.
One might object that belief alone does not guarantee good behaviour — a person may claim such a view yet act selfishly. That is true; the lesson therefore stresses practice ('सेवा एव पूजा'), not mere belief. On balance, however, sincerely seeing the divine in all does tend to soften the heart and loosen greed, so the statement is well supported by the lesson.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद, and illustrate with four examples drawn from this lesson.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the merging of sounds when two words (or word-parts) meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its parts. Examples from this lesson:
1. न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
2. समः + अहम् = समोऽहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि: ः + अ → ओ; the lost अ is marked by ऽ).
3. ईश्वरः + अर्जुन = ईश्वरोऽर्जुन (visarga before अ → ओ).
4. इदम् + सर्वम् = इदं सर्वम् (म् before a consonant → anusvara ं).
Being able to both join (सन्धि) and split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading Sanskrit verses such as those in this chapter correctly.

questions.question: Using words from this lesson, explain the six common विभक्ति (cases) with one example each.
questions.answer:
Sanskrit nouns change their endings to show their role:
1. प्रथमा (nominative, subject): ईशः 'the Lord', देवः 'god'.
2. द्वितीया (accusative, object): ईशम् / लवणम् 'salt (as object)'.
3. तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): भक्त्या 'by devotion'.
4. चतुर्थी (dative, 'for'): परोपकाराय-like 'for'; here सेवायै 'for service'.
5. पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from'): जलात् 'from water'.
6. षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): सर्वभूतानाम् 'of all beings'; सप्तमी (locative, 'in'): जले 'in the water', सर्वभूतेषु 'in all beings'.
Recognising these endings helps us understand who does what in a verse.

questions.question: Translate the following into simple English and explain: 'ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्। तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्॥'
questions.answer:
Translation: 'All this — whatever moves in this moving world — is pervaded by the Lord (ईश). Therefore enjoy (your share) through renunciation; do not covet anyone's wealth.'
Explanation: The first line states divine omnipresence — everything in the changing world is enveloped by ईश, so nothing is truly separate from the divine. The second line draws the practical lesson: since all belongs to the Lord, one should enjoy one's portion with a spirit of letting-go (त्याग) and contentment, and never greedily seize what belongs to others. The verse thus unites a vision of God-in-all with an ethic of non-greed.

questions.question: Compose a short Sanskrit paragraph (4–5 simple sentences, Devanagari) on the theme 'ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति', and give its English meaning.
questions.answer:
ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति। सः जले, स्थले, वृक्षे, पर्वते च वसति। सः सर्वभूतानां हृदये तिष्ठति। यः प्राणिषु दयां करोति सः ईशं भजते। अतः सेवा एव पूजा।
English: God is everywhere. He dwells in water, land, tree and mountain. He resides in the heart of all beings. One who shows compassion to living creatures worships God. Therefore, service itself is worship.
questions.explanation: Original simple composition using lesson vocabulary and grammar.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्।
तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्॥
(a) By whom is all this pervaded? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सर्वम्'. (c) What does 'मा गृधः' advise? (d) State the moral.
questions.answer: (a) All this is pervaded by ईश (the Lord). (b) सर्वम् = all/everything. (c) 'मा गृधः' advises us not to covet (another's wealth). (d) Moral: the divine pervades everything, so live with renunciation and non-greed.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्॥
(a) How is the Lord towards all beings? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'भक्त्या'. (c) Split by सन्धि-विच्छेद: 'समोऽहम्'. (d) What is the message?
questions.answer: (a) The Lord is समः (equal) towards all beings — none hateful, none favoured. (b) भक्त्या = 'by/with devotion' (instrumental). (c) समोऽहम् = समः + अहम्. (d) Message: God is equal to all; those who worship with devotion are one with God.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of Gita 9.29 with a sandhi split.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया॥
(a) Where does the Lord dwell? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'सर्वभूतानाम्'? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'हृद्देशे'. (d) What idea does this verse convey?
questions.answer: (a) The Lord dwells in the heart-region (हृद्देश) of all beings. (b) सर्वभूतानाम् is षष्ठी (genitive) plural — 'of all beings'. (c) हृद्देशे = 'in the heart-region' (locative). (d) It conveys that God is present within the heart of every creature.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of Gita 18.61 with case identification.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति॥
(a) What does the true devotee see? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सर्वत्र'. (c) What does the Lord promise such a devotee? (d) What value does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) He sees God everywhere and sees all things in God. (b) सर्वत्र = everywhere. (c) The Lord promises he is never lost to such a devotee, nor the devotee lost to Him. (d) Value: constant awareness of the divine in all — closeness through seeing God everywhere.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
गुरुः जलपात्रे लवणम् अक्षिपत्। श्वः शिष्यः लवणं न अपश्यत्, किन्तु जलम् आस्वादयत्। जलं लवणयुक्तम् आसीत्।
(a) What did the guru put in the water? (b) Could the pupil see it the next day? (c) How did the pupil know it was there? (d) What does this teach about ईश?
questions.answer: (a) The guru put salt (लवणम्) into the water. (b) No, the pupil could not see it. (c) He knew by taste — the water was salty (लवणयुक्तम्). (d) It teaches that ईश, though unseen, pervades everything, just like the dissolved salt.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
यः सर्वभूतेषु ईशं पश्यति, यः च प्राणिषु दयां करोति, सः एव सत्यम् ईशं भजते। सेवा एव पूजा।
(a) Who truly worships God? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दया'. (c) What is called the real पूजा here? (d) How can you apply this today?
questions.answer: (a) One who sees God in all beings and shows compassion to living creatures truly worships God. (b) दया = compassion/mercy. (c) सेवा (service) is called the real worship. (d) Application: help and be kind to people and animals, and serve those in need.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
वाक्यम् — 'ईशः सर्वत्र अस्ति; सः अदृश्यः, तथापि व्याप्तः।'
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'अदृश्यः'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'व्याप्तः'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नास्ति' (from न + अस्ति). (d) Translate the sentence.
questions.answer: (a) अदृश्यः = invisible. (b) व्याप्तः = pervaded/spread through. (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धि). (d) Translation: 'God is everywhere; He is invisible, yet He pervades all.'
questions.explanation: Comprehension with vocabulary, sandhi and translation.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
पाठे चत्वारः श्लोकाः सन्ति — ईशावास्योपनिषदः एकः, भगवद्गीतायाः त्रयः।
(a) How many verses are studied in the lesson? (b) From which Upanishad is one verse taken? (c) From which text are three verses taken? (d) Name any one verse's opening words.
questions.answer: (a) Four verses are studied. (b) One verse is from the Isha Upanishad (ईशावास्योपनिषद्). (c) Three verses are from the Bhagavad Gita. (d) e.g., 'ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम्' (or 'समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु', 'ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानाम्', 'यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र').
questions.explanation: Recall of the sources of the verses.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
वाक्यम् — 'ईशः जले वसति; ईशः सर्वभूतेषु तिष्ठति।'
(a) In which विभक्ति is 'जले'? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'सर्वभूतेषु'? (c) From which धातु is 'वसति'? (d) Translate the sentence.
questions.answer: (a) जले = सप्तमी (locative), 'in the water'. (b) सर्वभूतेषु = सप्तमी (locative) plural, 'in all beings'. (c) वसति is from the धातु वस् (to dwell). (d) Translation: 'God dwells in the water; God resides in all beings.'
questions.explanation: Comprehension with case and verb analysis.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
वाक्यम् — 'सेवा एव पूजा। यः दीनान् सेवते सः ईशं पूजयति।'
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सेवा'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दीनान्' (the poor/needy). (c) Translate the whole passage. (d) What is its moral?
questions.answer: (a) सेवा = service. (b) दीनान् = the poor/needy (accusative plural). (c) Translation: 'Service itself is worship. One who serves the needy worships God.' (d) Moral: serving the needy is the truest worship of the all-pervading ईश.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: service to the needy as worship.
